rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet does not state in plain outward language the inward secrets and realities that language cannot contain; his comprehensive station joins the Quran’s outward and inward realms.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى عدم تعبيره بلسان الظاهر عن أسرار الباطن والحقائق الآبية عن تصرف العبارات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet follows the Quran outwardly in its created dominion and inwardly in its unseen realm; Bursevi prays that believers follow the Quran in every age.
rows.anchor: يتبع بظاهره ملكه وبباطنه ملكوته نسأل الله سبحانه أن يجعلنا من المتبعين للقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā resumes and completes the discourse begun earlier.
rows.anchor: عود إلى تكملة ما ابتدىء به الكلام يعني نه نانست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People love the swiftly passing present world.
rows.anchor: أي الدنيا يعني دنياي شتاب كننده را

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They leave the afterlife by doing no work for it and denying it.
rows.anchor: فلا تعملون لها بل تنكرونها

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading contrasts love of worldly sensual pleasure with neglect of the afterlife’s blessing of obscurity.
rows.anchor: تحبون نعمة شهوة الدنيا وتذرون نعمة خمول الآخرة والخطاب للأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāḍira describes fresh, beautiful, soft, flourishing skin and appearance.
rows.anchor: النضرة طراوة البشرة وجمالها وذلك من أثر التنعم والناضر الغض الناعم من كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sincere believers’ faces at the Resurrection are radiant and joyful, showing the glow of bliss.
rows.anchor: وجوه كثيرة وهي وجوه المؤمنين المخلصين يوم إذ تقوم القيامة بهية متهللة يشاهد عليها نضرة النعيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He supports the description of radiant faces with the verse describing the glow of bliss on faces.
rows.anchor: تعرف فيه وجوههم نضرة النعيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wujūh is the subject, nāḍira its predicate, and the time phrase is adverbial; an indefinite subject is acceptable because the passage is detailing faces.
rows.anchor: على أن وجوه مبتدأ وناضرة خبره ويومئذ منصوب باضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāẓira is a second predicate of wujūh, with ilā rabbihā attached to it.
rows.anchor: قوله ناظرة خبر ثان للمبتدأ وإلى ربها متعلق بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Looking is the turning of sight or inward perception toward apprehending and seeing something.
rows.anchor: والنظر تقليب البصر والبصيرة لإدراك الشي ورؤيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The outward exegetes take the faces’ looking as the eyes’ looking, naming the place for the state located there.
rows.anchor: والمراد بنظر الوجوه نظر العيون التي فيها بطريق ذكر المحل وإرادة الحال

rows.speaker: أهل الحال
rows.claim: For the people of spiritual realization, divine vision is not confined to bodily eyesight, and God is exalted beyond such limitation.
rows.anchor: وأما عند أهل الحال ف ينحصر النظر في البصر والإجاء القيد والله منزه عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the subtle realm, the inward becomes outward and all parts witness the Real as inward perception does; the body has no rule there, while heart and spirit do.
rows.anchor: بل ينقلب الباطن ظاهرا والظاهر بصرا بجميع الأجزاء فيشاهد الحق به كما يشاهد بالبصيرة في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: بزركى
rows.claim: An unnamed sage says the way opens from every direction once one passes beyond oneself.
rows.anchor: راه ازدكام جانب است كفت ازجانب تونيست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man facing execution asked al-Hajjāj to walk three steps with him, then invoked the right of their companionship and obtained pardon.
rows.anchor: إن الحجاج أراد قتل شخص فقال له لي إليك حاجة قال ما هي قال أريد أن أمشي معك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bāsira means intensely frowning and dark, with no trace of joy; these are the faces of unbelievers and hypocrites.
rows.anchor: أي شديدة العبوس مظلمة ليس عليها أثر السرور أصلا وهي وجوه الكفرة والمنافقين

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines basr as hastening something before its proper time.
rows.anchor: البسر الاستعجال بالشيء قبل أوانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term fits because the faces’ foreboding occurs before they reach Hell, anticipating what follows.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى حالهم قبل الانتهاء بهم إلى النار فخص لفظ البسر تنبيها على أن ذلك مع ما ينالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grim faces expect, from signs before them, that a crushing calamity will befall them.
rows.anchor: توقع أربابها بحسب الامارات والجملة خبر بعد خبر

rows.speaker: أبو حيان والطيبي
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān and al-Ṭībī prefer taking ẓann here as certainty rather than conjecture.
rows.anchor: تفسير الظن بمعنى اليقين ولا ينافيه أن المصدرية كما توهم

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: Al-Raḍī notes that the maṣdariyya particle can follow supposition or a verb conveying knowledge, despite an objection that it cannot follow pure verification.
rows.anchor: فإنها إنما لا تقع بعد فعل التحقق الصرف فأما بعد فعل الظن أو ما يؤدي معنى العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fāqira is a tremendous disaster that breaks the vertebrae; faqīr is related to the image of a back broken by poverty.
rows.anchor: داهية عظيمة تقصم فقار الظهر ومنه سمى الفقير فإن الفقر كسر فقار ظهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase conveys unbearable extremity; by contrast, radiant faces expect every good thing to be done to them.
rows.anchor: وهو كناية عن غاية الشدة وعدم القدرة على التحمل فهي توقع ذلك كما تتوقع الوجوه الناضرة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view identifies the calamity with being veiled from the vision of the Lord of lords.
rows.anchor: أصح آنست كه آن بلا حجابست ازرؤيت رب الأرباب

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The radiant faces look only to God because they turned away from the world toward Him; the gloomy faces suffer for turning toward the world and away from God.
rows.anchor: لا إلى غيره بسبب الإعراض عن الدنيا في هذا اليوم والإقبال على الله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another inward view makes radiant faces shine with holy light and bliss, while the grim faces darken amid Hell, horrors, and bad company.
rows.anchor: وجوه يومئذ ناضرة للتنور بنور القدس والاتصال بعالم النور والسرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes preferring the present world to the afterlife and calls people to heed death, which ends their tie to worldly immediacy.
rows.anchor: ردع عن إيثار العاجلة على الآخرة أي ارتدعوا عن ذلك وتنبهوا لما بين أيديكم من الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unexpressed feminine subject of balaghat is the soul, inferred from context though not previously mentioned.
rows.anchor: الضمير للنفس وإن لم يجر لها ذكر لأن الكلام الذي وقعت فيه يدل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tarāqī are bones around the hollow at the base of the neck on either side; reaching them marks the death rattle.
rows.anchor: وهي العظام المكتنفة لثغرة النحر عن يمين وشمال فإذا بلغت إليها يكون وقت الغرغرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At this point the rational soul, the human spirit, reaches the collarbones and death is imminent.
rows.anchor: إذا بلغت النفس الناطقة وهي الروح الإنساني أالي الصر وهي العظام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet seized and shook Abū Jahl at al-Baṭḥāʾ, warned him, and Abū Jahl boasted of his invulnerability; at Badr he was felled by the sons of ʿAfrāʾ and finished by Ibn Masʿūd.
rows.anchor: وروى إنه لما نزلت هذه الآية أخذ رسول الله بمجامع ثوب أبي جهل بالبطحاء وهزه مرة أو مرتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqaṣahu means to kill someone in place, while ajhaza means to finish off a wounded person who is near death.
rows.anchor: اقعصه قتله مكانه وأجهز على الجريح أثبت قتل وأسره وتمم عليه

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet called every community a Pharaoh and identified Abū Jahl as this community’s Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: وكان رسول الله عليه السلام يقول إن لكل أمة فرعونا وإن فرعون هذه الأمة أبو جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first reading is that a person will not be left alive without duties or recompense.
rows.anchor: أي يحيى حال كونه مهملا فلا يكلف ولا يجزي

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another reading is that a person will not be left in the grave without resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقيل أن يترك في قبره فلا يبعث سدى المهمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suda means neglected or idle; the source also cites Arabic idioms for needs left uncompleted.
rows.anchor: سدى المهمل يقال أسدبت أبلى أسداء أي ملتها وتقول أسديت حاجتي وسديتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the denial rebuts the assumption of no resurrection: giving humans capacities and actions without duties would imply divine approval of evil, contrary to wisdom.
rows.anchor: وتكرير الإنكار لحسبانها يتضمن تكرير إنكاره للحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly obligations distinguish believers from corruptors; since this cramped world is not the place of full recompense, resurrection must follow so each is repaid for their deeds.
rows.anchor: ولا يجعل المتقين كالفجار ويجازي كل نفس بما تسعى

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: A great Sufi says it is bad adab to demand the immediate results of one’s deeds and spiritual states in this world, whose nature does not promise them.
rows.anchor: وقد قال بعض الكبار من طلب تعجيل نتائج أعماله وأحواله في هذه الدار فقد أساء الأدب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers the supposed difficulty of restoration by pointing to the first creation as proof that resurrection can occur.
rows.anchor: فإن مداره لما كان استبعادهم للإعادة استدل على تحققها ببدء الخلق

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh regards this as a second proof of resurrection, and the interrogative as rebuke.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الشيخ هو استدلال على صحة البعث بدليل ثان والاستفهام بمعنى التوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuṭfa is a little or much amount of clear water; manī is the reproductive fluid of man and woman from which an animal is formed.
rows.anchor: والنطفة بالضم الماء الصافي قل أو كثر والمني ماء الرجل والمرأة أي ما خلق منه حيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With yāʾ, yumnā describes manī; with tāʾ, it describes nuṭfa, and in either case means poured into the womb.
rows.anchor: ويمنى بالياء صفة منى وبالتاء صفة نطفة بمعنى يصب ويراق في الرحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Minā is said to take its name from the blood of sacrificial animals poured there.
rows.anchor: لما يمنى فيها من دماء القرابين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording belittles the human’s lowly origin while displaying God’s power to turn it into a well-formed person.
rows.anchor: نبه سبحانه بهذا على خسة قدر الإنسان أولا وكمال أقدرته ثانيا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view says yumnā emphasizes the human’s contemptible origin and asks how such a creature can rebel against God; the wording hints at an indecent fact, as in the statement that Jesus and Mary ate food.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم فائدة قوله يمنى للإشارة إلى حقارة حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deterrent aspect of punishment operates in this world: hearing about afterlife punishment restrains people from actions that lead to it.
rows.anchor: فإن ذلك لا يصور في الآخرة بل في الدنيا فإن العقوبة الأخروية تنكل من سمعها وتمنعه من تعاطي ما يؤدي إليها

rows.speaker: التأويلات القاشانية
rows.claim: The Qashānī inward reading sees Pharaoh contesting the Real through manifest selfhood clothed in pride; God subdued and cast him into Hell, as in the saying that pride is God’s mantle.
rows.anchor: نازع الحق بشدة ظهور أنانيته في رداء الكبرياء فقهر وقذف في النار ملعونا

rows.speaker: البقلي
rows.claim: Al-Baqlī says Pharaoh’s false claim disgraced him in both worlds, as happens to anyone claiming spiritual stations they do not possess.
rows.anchor: افتضح في الدنيا والآخرة وهكذا كل ما يدعي ما ليس له من المقامات

rows.speaker: بشر
rows.claim: Bishr says God let Pharaoh’s tongue utter grand claims while emptying them of their realities.
rows.anchor: قال بشر انطق الله لسانه بالعريض من الدعاوي وإخلاء عن حقائقها

rows.speaker: السري
rows.claim: Al-Sarī says a servant who dresses as a master becomes a warning; Pharaoh’s claim to lordship was refuted by everything, even himself.
rows.anchor: العبد إذا تزيى بزي السيد صار نكالا ألا ترى كيف ذكر الله

rows.speaker: موسى
rows.claim: A report in al-Wasīṭ says Moses asked why Pharaoh was spared for 400 years while claiming divinity and resisting the messengers; God replied that Pharaoh was good-natured and easy to approach, so He repaid him in this world.
rows.anchor: وفي الوسيط عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report explains the worldly recompense for a disbeliever’s good deeds, whereas a believer receives most of their reward in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: فأردت إن أكافئه أي مكافأة دنيوية وكذا حسنات كل كافر وإما المؤمن فأكثر ثوابه في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account indicates that Pharaoh died an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: ودلت الآية على أن فرعون مات كافرا

rows.speaker: الفتوحات المكية
rows.claim: The Futūḥāt al-Makkiyya says Pharaoh and Nimrod remain in Hell eternally.
rows.anchor: فرعون ونمرود مؤبدان في النار انتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi treats the Shaykh’s other statements as dialectical discussion and warns against prolonged debate, which he calls severe misguidance.
rows.anchor: محمول على المباحثة فصن لسانك عن الإطالة فإنها من أشد ضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi notes that Pharaoh’s two claims, forty years apart, make it likely that highest lordship meant divinity; reading it merely as political supremacy proves little, since rulers and materialists need not claim divinity.
rows.anchor: صدر من فرعون كلمتان الأولى قوله أنا ربكم الأعلى والثانية قوله ما عملت لكم من إله غيري وبينهما على ما قيل أربعون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That refers to Pharaoh’s story and what God did to him.
rows.anchor: أي فيما ذكر من قصة فرعون وما فعل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one disposed to fear is one with knowledge: a knower of God and His attributes fears Him and does not rebel against God or His messengers lest punishment descend.
rows.anchor: إن العارف بالله وبشؤونه يخشى منه فلا يتمرد على الله ولا على أنبيائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wise person learns from another’s fate rather than waiting to suffer the same consequence.
rows.anchor: والعاقل من وعظ بغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian admonitory poem urges the hearer to turn from punishment toward pardon and leave heedlessness before shame arrives.
rows.anchor: تويش ازعقوبت در عفو كوب كه سودى تدارد فغان زير وب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing Meccan deniers, the rhetorical question challenges their claim that resurrection is difficult: creating the immense, wondrous sky is harder by their reckoning, so restoring people is within God’s power.
rows.anchor: خطاب لأهل مكة المنكرين للبعث بناء على صعوبته في زعمهم بطريق التوبيخ والتبكيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison follows the statement that resurrection requires only one blast, underscoring its ease for God.
rows.anchor: فإنما هى زجرة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question seeks their admission that the heavens are harder to create, forcing them to concede that the easier resurrection is possible.
rows.anchor: وهو استفهام تقرير ليقروا بأن خلق السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Antum is the subject, ashadd its predicate, khalqan a specification, and al-samāʾ is coordinated with antum with its predicate elided.
rows.anchor: قوله أأنتم مبتدأ وأشد خبره وخلقا تمييز والسماء عطف على أنتم وحذف خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Banāhā resumes the sentence and details how the sky was created; the clause can begin after a pause at al-samāʾ, with am as a connected alternative.
rows.anchor: وهو استئناف وتفصيل لكيفية خلقها المستفاد من قوله أم السماء فيتم الكلام حينئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the sky a building rather than a roof highlights its resistance to disorder and collapse, despite building usually naming lower structures.
rows.anchor: واستعمل البناء في موضع السقف فإن السماء سقف مرفوع والبناء إنما يستعمل في أسافل البناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This explains the building: God made the sky’s rise from earth into the heights vast, a distance of five hundred years’ journey.
rows.anchor: بيان للبناء أي جعل مقدار ارتفاعها من الأرض وذهابها إلى سمت العلو

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view defines samk as the sky’s thickness, the distance between its lower and upper surfaces, likewise a five-hundred-year journey.
rows.anchor: السمك الارتفاع الذي بين سطح السماء الأسفل الذي يلينا وسطحها الأعلى

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib derives aghṭasha from the description of a partly dim eye; it can mean making dark or becoming dark, and the transitive sense applies here.
rows.anchor: يقال أغطشه الله إذا جعله مظلما وأغطش الليل إذا صار مظلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aghṭasha can be transitive or intransitive; the intended reading is that God made the night dark.
rows.anchor: وأغطش الليل إذا صار مظلما فهو متعد ولازم والأول هو المراد هنا أي جعله مظلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although night denotes the time of darkness, the phrase is not redundant: God’s decree and governance cause the darkness of that time.
rows.anchor: فقوله واغطش ليلها يرجع معناه إلى أنه جعل المظلم مظلما وهو يعيد والجواب معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akhraja ḍuḥāhā means that God brought out the daylight; ḍuḥā can denote sunlight or its morning period.
rows.anchor: أي أبرز نهارها عبر عنه بالضحى وهو ضوء الشمس ووقت الضحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The daylight is named for ḍuḥā, when the sun’s power and brilliance are greatest, the most fitting time to mention in a passage of blessing.
rows.anchor: وهو الوقت الذي تشرق فيه الشمس ويقوم سلطانها لأنه أشرف أوقاتها وأطيبها على تسمية المحل باسم أشرف ما حل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning light after darkness makes the blessing more complete, and the sky is named as the locus because its motion is connected to their occurrence.
rows.anchor: فإن إضافة النور بعد الظلمة أتم في الأنعام وأكمل في الإحسان وإضافة الليل والضحى إلى السماء لدوران حدوثها على حركتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attribution of ḍuḥā to the sky can be understood through the sun, with an implied sun’s light; the term still points to the period of full solar authority.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون إضافة الضحى إليها بواسطة الشمس أي أبرز ضوء شمسها بتقدير المضاف

rows.speaker: إمام زاهد
rows.claim: Imām Zāhid says worldly day and night result from the motion of the sun and moon in the sky.
rows.anchor: إمام زاهد فرموده كه روز وشب دنيا بآسمان يدا كردد بسب آفرينش شرتاب وماه دور

rows.speaker: بعض العارفين
rows.claim: Some gnostics portray night as male and day as female: night covers day, she bears the entities, and bringing day from night resembles bringing Eve from Adam.
rows.anchor: قال بعض العارفين الليل ذكر والنهار أنثى فلما تغشاها الليل حملت فولدت فظهرت الكائنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Direct address intensifies the reproach, like a complainant turning to confront the person who wronged him; no one could make the Prophet know the man’s inner state.
rows.anchor: لذلك فإن المشافهة أدخل في تشديد العتبا كمن يشكو إلى الناس جانيا جنى عليه ثم يقبل على الجاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pause is appropriate after this question: what follows is a new statement, not its object.
rows.anchor: أي لا يدريك شيء فتم الكلام عنده فيوقف عليه وليس ما بعده مفعوله بل هو ابتداء كلام

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhaylī observes that the passage first reports the incident in third person, then turns to direct address, mirroring the Prophet’s initial turning away before addressing him to console him.
rows.anchor: قال الامام السهيلي رحمه الله ، انظر كيف نزلت الآية بلفظ الأخبار عن الغائب

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhaylī says the Prophet hoped for the conversion of the pagan, identified as al-Walīd or Umayya, whose Islam might have brought many others to Islam.
rows.anchor: وهو الوليد أو أمية وكان مثله يسلم بإسلامه بشر كثير فكلم نبيه عليه السلام

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhaylī notes that Ibn Umm Maktūm was already Muslim and had learned his religious essentials, while the pagans had not accepted Islam.
rows.anchor: وأما أولئك الكفار فما كانوا قد أسلموا وكان إسلامهم سببا لإسلام جمع عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the Prophet sought a greater benefit, his action outwardly suggested preferring the rich and disregarding the poor man’s hurt, so God reproached him for leaving the better course.
rows.anchor: إلا أن ظاهر ما فعله الرسول عليه السلام يوهم تقديم الأغنياء على الفقراء وقلة المبالاة بانكسار قلوب الفقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yazzakkā is contracted from yatazakkā and means that the blind man may purify himself through what he learns from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: بتشديدين أصله يتزكى أي يتطهر بما يقتبس منك من أوضار الأوزار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God knows the outcome, laʿalla in speech of the mighty can express certainty; alternatively it conveys hope from the Prophet’s perspective to stress that neglecting a hoped-for seeker is impermissible.
rows.anchor: وكلمة لعل مع تحقق التزكي وارد على سنن الكبرياء فإن لعل في كلام العظماء يراد به القطع والتحقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yadhakkaru is contracted from yatadhakkaru and means that the man may take heed.
rows.anchor: بتشديدين أيضا أصله يتذكر والتذكر هو الاتعاظ يعني باخود ند كيرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If he does not reach complete purification, the Prophet’s exhortation may still benefit him.
rows.anchor: أي فتنفعه موعظتك إن لم يبلغ درجة التزكي التام

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf explains that the Prophet could not know whether the man would attain purification or recollection; if he had known, he would not have neglected him.
rows.anchor: المعنى إنك لا تدري ما هو مترقب منه من تزكى أو تذكر ولو دريت لما فرط ذلك منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seeker comes quickly, eager for the guidance, religious rulings, and good qualities available from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أي حال كونه مسرعا طالبا لما عندك من أحكام الرشد وخصال الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seeker may fear God, or fear the disbelievers as he comes to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: الله تعالى أو يخشى الكفار وإذا هم أتيانك

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Saʿdī al-Muftī sees an ellipsis by ihtibāk: mentioning the rich first implies the poor, while the seeker’s coming and fear imply their opposites in the first clause.
rows.anchor: ذكر الغنى أولا للدلالة على الفقر ثانيا والمجيء والخشية ثانيا للدلالة على ضدهما أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form drops one of the two tāʾs for ease; its underlying form is tata-lahhā.
rows.anchor: بحذف إحدى التاءين تخفيفا أي تتلهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means turning away or being occupied from something, not playing with something; the latter sense would not suit the Prophet’s rank.
rows.anchor: من لهى عن الشيء بكسر الهاء يلهى لهيا اعرض عنه لا من لهوت بالشيء بالفتح ألهو لهوا إذا لعبت به

rows.speaker: بعض التفاسير
rows.claim: Some tafsirs allow a play-related sense, treating engagement with heedless people as useless play; Bursevi rejects this because it would make preaching vain, though the Prophet engaged them only to guide them.
rows.anchor: ولو أخذ من اللهو وجعل التشاغل بأهل التغافل من جنس اللهو واللعب لكونه عبثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting anta before both verbs focuses the rebuke on the Prophet in particular: someone of his rank should not pursue the self-sufficient and neglect the poor seeker.
rows.anchor: أي مثلك خصوصا لا ينبغي أن يتصدى للمستغنى ويتلهى عن الفقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The placement of lahū and ʿanhu hints at the Prophet’s concern with the people indicated by each pronoun.
rows.anchor: للتعريض باهتمامه عليه السلام ، بمضمونهما تنبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account teaches that worth lies in souls and spiritual states, not outward appearance or wealth: faith makes the socially lowly noble, while unbelief makes the socially esteemed wretched.
rows.anchor: حيث أفادت القصة أن العبرة بالأرواح والأحوال لا بالأشباح والأموال والعزيز من أعزه الله بالإيمان والطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet thereafter never frowned at a poor person or sought out a rich one, and the poor held an honored place in his gathering.
rows.anchor: روى إنه عليه السلام ما بعس بعد ذلك في وجه ففير قط ولا تصدى لغني وكان الفقراء في مجلسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode instructs scholars, judges, and rulers to draw a weak seeker of good near and prefer him over a prominent person lacking good.
rows.anchor: فحملة الشرع والعلم والحكام مخاطبون في تقريب الضعيف من أهل الخير وتقديمه على الشريف العاري عن الخير

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the passage honors poverty and its people while devaluing worldly status; companionship with sincere, detached poor people benefits, unlike companionship with the rich.
rows.anchor: بين الله درجة الفقر وتعظيم أهله وخسة الدنيا وتحقير أهلها

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A hadith says that favoring a rich person by treating a poor person unjustly destroys a third of one’s religion.
rows.anchor: من تحامل على فقير لغني فقد هدم ثلث دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taḥāmala can mean enduring something with difficulty, or treating another person unjustly.
rows.anchor: تحاملت على الشيء إذا تكلفت الشيء على مشقة وتحامل فلان على فلان إذا لم يعدل

rows.speaker: بعض الأكابر
rows.claim: Some great Sufis explain that the Prophet honored Quraysh’s chiefs as manifestations of divine majesty, while a higher station is to see no distinction among people under God’s absolute reality.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الأكابر إنما كان صلى الله عليه وسلم يتواضع لأكابر قريش لأن الأعزاء من الخلائق مظهر لعزة الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The higher instruction is to remain with those who call on God morning and evening, as stated later in the Quran.
rows.anchor: وهو ما أمره الله به آخرا بعدما صدر سورة عبس في قوله واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشى

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: Bursevi invokes the divine saying about the hungry and thirsty person whom people failed to feed and give drink.
rows.anchor: كما قال جعت فلم تطعمني وظمئت فلم تسقني الحديث كم افي الجواهر للشعراني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On either interpretation, the fāʾ gives detail, because the implied meaning already contains the action it explicates.
rows.anchor: وعلى الوجهين فالفاء للتفصيل فإن التقدير يتضمنه عى المعنيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the bodily reading, God makes birth possible by opening the previously closed womb and directing the infant to turn head down.
rows.anchor: أي سهل مخرجه من البطن بأن فتح فم الرحم وكان غير مفتوح قبل الولادة وألهمه أن ينتكس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the moral reading, God makes paths of good and evil accessible by granting capacity, explaining benefit and harm, reason, prophets, and revealed books.
rows.anchor: أو يسر له سبيل الخير والشر في الدين ومكنه من السلوك فيهما وذلك بالأقدار والتعريف له بما هو نافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite form al-sabīl rather than a possessive phrase signals generality: it applies to humans and jinn in the moral reading, and animals too in the birth reading.
rows.anchor: وتعريف السبيل باللام دون الإضافة بأن يقال سبيله للإشعار بعمومه لأنه عام للأنس والجن

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says God makes the path easy for the person destined for success, so that they seek right guidance and salvation.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله يسر على من قدر له التوفيق طلب رشده واتباع نجاته

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr ibn Ṭāhir says God makes easy for each person what He created and decreed for them.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن طاهر رحمه الله يسر على كل أحد ما خلقه له وقدره عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God takes the person’s soul when the appointed term is complete.
rows.anchor: أي قبض روحه عند تمام أجله المقدر المسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides a grave as an honor, rather than leaving the body exposed for beasts and birds to tear apart.
rows.anchor: جعله في قبر يواري فيه تكرمة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qabara is to bury by one’s own hand; qābir is the burier and qabr the grave, while aqbara means to command or enable burial.
rows.anchor: يقال قبر الميت إذا دفنه بيده والقابر هو الدافن والقبر هو مقر الميت وأقبره إذ أمر بدفنه

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-Asrār says God did not leave the body for beasts or cremation; burial is among the honors granted to Muslims.
rows.anchor: لم يجعله مما يطرح للسباع أو يلقى للنواويس

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib explains aqbara as giving someone a place in which to be buried, like giving water to draw from, or as inspiring burial.
rows.anchor: أقبرته جعلت له مكانا يقبر فيه نحو أسقيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muqbir is God because He commands burial in graves.
rows.anchor: فالمقبر هو الله لأنه الآمر بالدفن في القبور

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: The Mathnawī passage says crafts, including the know-how of burial, originated in revelation and were then developed by human reason.
rows.anchor: جمله حرفتها يقين ازوحى بود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death is a blessing for the believer because it frees them from the prison of this world and joins them to everlasting life and bliss.
rows.anchor: وعد الأماتة من النعم بالنسبة إلى المؤمن فإن بالموت يتخلص من سجن الدنيا وأيضا إن شأن الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the unbeliever, death is the key to distress because of false belief and bad deeds.
rows.anchor: وإنما كان مفتاح كلا بلاء ومحنة في حق الكافر من سوء اعتقاده وسيئات أعماله

rows.speaker: بعض التفاسير
rows.claim: Some tafsirs include death either because it precedes burial or to warn that worldly life is temporary and ends in death.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض التفاسير ذكر الأماتة إما لأنها مقدمة الأقبار وإما للتخويف والتذكير بأن الحياة الدنيوية فانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian verse says every human from Adam onward falls short of fulfilling divine commands and should apologize for that failure, since no one can fully render God’s due.
rows.anchor: مراد همه آدميانند از آدم تاباين غايت وهركز هي آدمى از عهده حقوق اداي اوامر إلهي

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmī reading says people have not fulfilled the command to manifest the realities of God’s names and the virtues of His attributes.
rows.anchor: من الإتيان بمواجب حقوقنا من الظهور بحقائق أسمائنا والقيام بفضائل صفاتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage begins counting the blessings that preserve life, following the earlier account of blessings involved in human origination.
rows.anchor: شروع في تعداد النعم المتعلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should consider their food and how God has arranged their sustenance.
rows.anchor: أي فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه الذي عليه يدور أمر معاشه كيف دبرناه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says looking at one’s food teaches the lowliness of one’s status and the shortness of one’s life.
rows.anchor: فلينظر الإنسان إلى طعامه ليعلم خسة قدره وفناء عمره

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A hadith makes Adam’s food an example of the world: even after seasoning and salting it, one should see what it ultimately becomes.
rows.anchor: إن مطعم ابن آدم جعله الله مثلا للدنيا وإن قزحه وملحه فنظر إلى ماذا يصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qazzaḥa means adding spices to a pot; qizāḥ is seasoning, and malaḥa means adding salt.
rows.anchor: يقال قزح القدر جعل التابل فيها وهو كصاحب وهاجر إبزار الطعام وملحها جعل الملح فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pouring is the ample descent of needed rain from clouds.
rows.anchor: أنزلنا إنزالا وافيا من السحاب أي الغيث وهو المطر المحتاج إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is a badal ishtimāl from food, since water causes food to grow; the resumptive pronoun is omitted, understood as poured for it.
rows.anchor: بدل اشتمال من طعامه لأن الماء سبب لحدوث الطعام فالثاني مشتمل على الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammar does not require the replaced expression itself to contain the substitute; the second item can encompass the first.
rows.anchor: إذ لا يلزم فيه أن يكون المبدل منه مشتملا على البدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the rain, God split the soil for the plants; thumma marks that the splitting follows the pouring.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الشق بعد الصب أورد كلمة ثم الشق بالفارسية شكافتن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaqqan is a wondrous splitting suited to the plants’ differing sizes, shapes, and forms.
rows.anchor: بديعا لائقا بما يشقها من النبات صغرا وكبرا وشكلا وهيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fīhā refers to the earth split by the plants, and the fāʾ marks succession.
rows.anchor: أي في الأرض المشقوقة بالنبات والفاء للتعقيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥabb refers collectively to harvested grains such as wheat and barley, and can denote either a little or a lot.
rows.anchor: والحب كل ما حصد من نحو الحنطة والشعير وغيرهما وهو جنس الحبة كالتمر والتمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grain comes first because it is the basic foundation of food.
rows.anchor: فيشمل القليل والكثير قدمه لأنه الأصل في الغذاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿInaban is coordinated with ḥabban; coordination does not require the two items to share every qualification, so no difficulty follows if grape growth is not described by the same soil-splitting.
rows.anchor: {وعنبا} عطف على حبا وليس من لوازم العطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference is to the grapevine as it first emerges from earth; grape and olive are named by their fruits because they are famous for them and their fruits are eaten directly.
rows.anchor: فإن المراد هنا شجرة العنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grapes are singled out among fruits because they both delight as fruit and nourish as food, and are among the most wholesome foods.
rows.anchor: وأفرد العنب بالذكر من بين الثمار لأنه فاكهة من وجه يتلذذ به وطعام من وجه يتغذى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaḍban is fresh green fodder, identified as alfalfa, called asista in Persian and al-isfist in Arabicized form.
rows.anchor: أي رطبة وهي نبات يقال له الفصفصة وبالفارسية اسست ومعربه الاسفست
